plan: My value is $24. In a first-price sealed bid auction with three bidders, I want to bid strategically. Since values are randomly drawn, other bidders might bid near their own values. A safe strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. I'll aim to bid around $22-$23, which gives me room to win if others bid lower, while protecting against overpaying. This balanced approach minimizes the risk of paying more than the item's worth.

My private value is $16. In a first-price sealed bid auction with three bidders, I want to bid strategically. Since values are drawn randomly between $0-$49, a pure "bid your value" strategy isn't optimal. I'll aim to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. Given the random nature, I'll bid around 80-90% of my value to create a buffer. This gives me a chance to win while protecting against overpaying.

My value is $24. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is often to bid close to my true value. Since other bidders' values are randomly drawn, they might bid higher or lower. I'll bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer. A bid around $23.5 protects against overpaying while still having a good chance of winning if my value is competitive. This strategy minimizes the risk of paying more than the item is worth to me.
